summary: England and Wales and Northern Ireland have no forced heirship, but a court can order provision for close family. Scotland protects spouse and children with legal rights over movable estate. Trusts are fully recognised; there is no private foundation.
family_claims: England and Wales: Inheritance (Provision for Family and Dependants) Act 1975; Northern Ireland: 1979 Order. Scotland instead has fixed legal rights: spouse and children each take 1/3 (with both) or 1/2 of the movable estate, Succession (Scotland) Act 1964 ss. 8-10.
foreign_law_note: Movables follow the law of the deceased's domicile (which can stay foreign), immovables follow the law of their location. Nationality is irrelevant and there is no choice of law as such.
trust_note: Hague Trusts Convention in force for the UK since 1 January 1992. Trusts are taxed: 20% entry charge above the nil-rate band, 6% every ten years on relevant property. No private foundation form; charitable incorporated organisations exist.
open_questions: Current rates of trust and inheritance tax were not rechecked.

The HCCH status-table page could be read only in an older cached version that does not show territorial extensions; extension dates come from the UK Treaty Series 14 (1992) and a Dutch treaty record, and should be re-checked on hcch.net.
